item.title: Non-invasive oral magnetoelectric vagus nerve neuromodulation for Parkinson’s disease therapy
item.content:encoded:
Nature Biomedical Engineering, Published online: 03 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41551-026-01829-x

Orally delivered magnetoelectric particles activate vagal afferent fibres in the gut−brain axis and influence neurodegeneration and neuroinflammation in mouse models of Parkinson’s disease.
item.dc:title: Non-invasive oral magnetoelectric vagus nerve neuromodulation for Parkinson’s disease therapy

item.title: Re-timing mortality risk through individualized modelling of lifespan trajectories
item.content:encoded:
Nature Biomedical Engineering, Published online: 02 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41551-026-01822-4

RetiME is a deep learning-based biomarker that maps retinal features to individual mortality risks and can reconstruct personalized lifespan trajectories associated with observed mortality outcomes with distinct disease-related mortality patterns.
item.dc:title: Re-timing mortality risk through individualized modelling of lifespan trajectories

item.title: A single-step injectable Janus-adhesive hydrogel for endoscopic gastrointestinal fistula repair
item.content:encoded:
Nature Biomedical Engineering, Published online: 30 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41551-026-01820-6

A thermoresponsive hydrogel sealant, prepared in a user-friendly and single-step process, and featuring Janus-type adhesion, is injected endoscopically and repairs gastrointestinal fistulas in rat and minipig models.
item.dc:title: A single-step injectable Janus-adhesive hydrogel for endoscopic gastrointestinal fistula repair

item.title: Closing the loop on blood flow control in spinal cord injury
item.content:encoded:
Nature Biomedical Engineering, Published online: 29 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41551-026-01784-7

After spinal cord injury, clinicians raise blood pressure to protect tissue without directly monitoring the effect on the cord, exposing patients to harm. We designed a closed-loop controller that adjusts drug infusion in response to ultrasonography-based measurements of spinal cord blood flow, stabilizing perfusion at the injury site and preserving neurological function in animals.
item.dc:title: Closing the loop on blood flow control in spinal cord injury
item.dc:source: Nature Biomedical Engineering, Published online: 2026-10-29; | doi:10.1038/s41551-026-01784-7

item.title: Optimal closed-loop feedback control of blood flow after spinal cord injury with norepinephrine
item.content:encoded:
Nature Biomedical Engineering, Published online: 29 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41551-026-01777-6

A closed-loop control strategy regulates spinal cord blood flow by adjusting norepinephrine infusion using real-time flow measurements, enabling direct flow targeting after acute injury.
item.dc:title: Optimal closed-loop feedback control of blood flow after spinal cord injury with norepinephrine
